correctness.rationale: For symmetric sources z±=r exp(±ia), averaging their measures bounds the smaller, and its strictly analytic even density H has a reflection-invariant superlevel set, so bathtub rearrangement attains this bound with both measures equal. Writing u=cos t, H=C(k−cu)/[u²−2kcu+k²−sin²a]; derivative numerator q=cu²−2ku+c(k²+sin²a) is strictly decreasing in u, giving one/two maxima and c*=(sqrt(k²+8)−k)/2. The exact factorization H(u)−H(1)=−C(k−c)(u−1)(u−[kc+c²−1])/[Q(u)Q(1)] yields ρc=acos(kc+c²−1)/π. Unique (mod null sets) two reflected superlevel arcs for a>acos c*, ρ<ρc, and central arc elsewhere. A Poisson interval integral decreases with circular distance, making central midpoint the best connected arc. Local arccos expansion gives square-root merger. Independently verified q and crossing factor with symbolic polynomial operations; finite grid tests cannot prove continuum uniqueness.
